body.p: Claims 1-7 are pending in the application. New Claims 8-10 have been presented for the Examiner's consideration. Reconsideration of the rejections set forth in the aforementioned Office Action is respectfully requested in view of the above amended and new claims, and following remarks. The basis for these amended and new claims can be found throughout the specification, claims and drawings as originally filed.

Applicant's representative wishes to acknowledge and appreciates the courtesies and assistance extended during the recent interview with the Examiner. The discussions proved fruitful in clarifying Applicant's claimed disclosure and the Examiner's positions. The above amended and new claims, and following remarks reflect those discussed with and suggested by the Examiner during the interview.

Applicant respectfully submits that the above amended and new claims overcome the current rejections of record and, as such, all of the claims are now in condition for allowance. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests completion of prosecution and issuance of a Notice of Allowance. However, should the Examiner elect to issue an Office Action in response to this Amendment, Applicant hereby requests a telephonic interview with the Examiner prior to issuance of any Office Action in order to discuss any remaining issues.

During the interview, the Examiner noted that the claims contain "subjective language" (e.g., "relief"). Applicant respectfully disagrees with this characterization. For example, the term "relief" for a person includes, at least, traveling a vehicle to a place
where a person requiring relief is located and then sending that person to a destination place. See, for example, Applicant's application at page 8, lines 16-19 and page 13, lines 15-23.

Claims 1-7 have been interpreted under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), sixth paragraph; as such, the claims have been interpreted to cover the corresponding structure described in the specification that achieves the claimed function, and equivalents thereof. The absence of the word "means" (or "step for") in a claim creates a rebuttable presumption that the claim element is not to be treated in accordance with 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), sixth paragraph. The word "means" (or "step for") is absent from Applicant's claims. As such, Applicant respectfully traverses this allegation and respectfully disagrees with this characterization.

Applicant respectfully submits that "a center device" corresponds to a center device 50. As shown in FIG. 1, a measure determination device 60 is provided in the center device 50. The measure determination device 60 includes a microcomputer having a CPU and a semiconductor memory such as RAM or ROM. Therefore, the center device 50 incudes at least one processor and a memory coupled to the at least one processor.

Additionally, "a vehicle control device" corresponds to an autonomous driving device 20 and an autonomous driving device 30. According to Applicant's specification, "one of the plurality of autonomous driving devices 20 is provided as a main control device, and the other one of the plurality of autonomous driving devices 30 is provided as a sub control device" and "[t]he control units 21 and 31 respectively include CPUs 22 and

32 and microcomputers each having a semiconductor memory (hereinafter, memory 23 and 33) such as RAM or ROM." As such, each of the autonomous driving device 20 and the autonomous driving device 30 include a processor and a memory. Therefore, the vehicle control device includes at least one processor and a memory coupled to the at least one processor.

As previously discussed, Applicant does not intend to have the claims treated under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), sixth paragraph. While Applicant disagrees with the Examiner's assertion that the noted claim elements invoke claim interpretation under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), sixth paragraph, in the interest of advancing and expediting prosecution, and without prejudice to pursuing this and related subject matter in future applications, Applicant has amended Claims 1-7 pursuant to the Examiner's suggestions and recommendations.

As such, Applicant respectfully submits that the claims, taken together as a whole, recite sufficient structure, material or acts to entirely perform the claimed function so as to preclude the application of 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), sixth paragraph. Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner's interpretation in this regard too narrowly defines Applicant's claimed disclosure and that Applicant's claimed disclosure could be characterized more broadly. Accordingly, reconsideration of the interpretation of the noted claim elements is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-7 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), first paragraph as "failing to comply with the written description requirement. The claim(s)

contains subject matter which was not described in the specification in such a way as to reasonably convey to one skilled in the relevant art that the inventor or a joint inventor, or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the inventor(s), at the time the application was filed, had possession of the claimed invention." Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection as it is Applicant's view that the claims as written fully comply with Section 112. However, in the interest of advancing and expediting prosecution, and without prejudice to pursuing this and related subject matter in future applications, Applicant has amended Claims 1-7 pursuant to the Examiner's suggestions and recommendations. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the Section 112(a) or Section 112 (pre-AIA), first paragraph rejection to Claims 1-7.

Claims 1-7 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph as "being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention." Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection as it is Applicant's view that the claims as written fully comply with Section 112. However, in the interest of advancing and expediting prosecution, and without prejudice to pursuing this and related subject matter in future applications, Applicant has amended Claims 1-7 pursuant to the Examiner's suggestions and recommendations. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the Section 112(b) or Section 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph rejection to Claims 1-7.

Claims 1-7 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poeppel et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2023/0205202 in view of Wilson et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0361451. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's characterization that Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, renders Applicant's claimed disclosure obvious. Additionally, there is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. It is respectfully submitted that Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, teaches away from Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device. Applicant's claimed disclosure recites an improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device having a unique and advantageous orientation and combination of components which are more efficient, advantageous, and eliminate various negative features associated with the devices/systems disclosed in the cited references.

Applicant's claimed disclosure is directed toward an improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device which maintain safety and appropriately provide relief to a failed autonomous driving vehicle. Applicant's improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device are able to accomplish these tasks as a result of their unique and advantageous arrangement and orientation of components and features which include, in part, the following:

Feature A: a center device placed outside an autonomous driving vehicle and a vehicle control device placed to the autonomous driving vehicle, and the center device and the vehicle control device wirelessly communicate with each other;
Feature B: a type of a passenger of a target vehicle includes types of a passenger classified based on a degree of assistance required for a relief to the passenger;
Feature C: a first stop position decided by the center device and a second stop position decided by the vehicle control device; and

Feature D: a vehicle control device causes the target vehicle to head to the second stop position, which has been decided by the vehicle control device placed on the target vehicle, in a case where the first stop position is not acquired from the center device, and causes the target vehicle to head to the first stop position in a case where the first stop position is acquired from the center device.
Poeppel et al. describes systems and methods for remote status detection of autonomous vehicles.
Wilson describes a system and a method for rendezvous coordination of an autonomous automotive vehicle with an ambulance.

Wilson describes "[s]tep 308 analyzes the data gathering from the monitoring step 304 to determine whether the passenger of the autonomous automotive vehicle is potentially experiencing a medical emergency situation."
However, there are at least two points which should be noted.
First, Poeppel et al. describes "[t]he vehicle rendezvous coordination method starts in step 300 of FIG. 3A. It is implemented by a computer system within the autonomous
automotive vehicle which includes wireless communications capabilities." Therefore, Step 308 is performed within a vehicle.

Applicant's acquisition of a type of a passenger as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 5-7 of Applicant's claimed disclosure is performed by a center device, which is located outside the vehicle (see Feature A).
Second, according to Feature B, the type of a passenger of the target vehicle is unrelated to a medical emergency situation.
Wilson describes a safe rendezvous location A and a safe rendezvous location B.

By contrast, as described in Feature C, a first stop position is set (decided) by a center device. A second stop position is set (decided) by a vehicle control device. According to this configuration, "the autonomous driving vehicle can be stopped at a stop position suitable for relief. On the other hand, even when the first stop position set by the center device cannot be obtained, such as when the communication between the autonomous driving vehicle and the center device is interrupted, the vehicle control device can cause the vehicle to stop at the second stop position which is autonomously set by the vehicle control device. Thus, the configuration can control the autonomous driving vehicle more safely." (As described in Applicant's specification).

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's "distributed computing options" characterization raised during the interview. Specifically, Applicant's claimed disclosure describes "simply setting a stop position for an autonomous driving vehicle does not take a circumstance for those who provides relief for the failed autonomous driving vehicle into consideration. Thus, an inappropriate stop position for relief may be set." In other words, when a failed autonomous driving vehicle sets a stop position, since
a circumstance for those who provide relief may not be considered, an inappropriate stop position for relief may be set.

In addition, Applicant's claimed disclosure describes "when the first stop position set by the center device can be acquired, the autonomous driving vehicle can stop at the first stop position. When the first stop position set by the center device cannot be acquired, the autonomous driving vehicle can stop at the second stop position. Therefore, the stop position of the autonomous driving vehicle can be changed at the convenience of the manager who manages the center device, that is, the person who provides relief."

Moreover, in order to more clearly describe/distinguish the first and second stop positions, Feature D has been added to amend independent Claims 1 and 5-7 of Applicant's claimed disclosure. That is, contrary to the cited prior art references, independent Claims 1 and 5-7 of Applicant's claimed disclosure have been amended so as to more clearly recite that the first stop position is given preference over the second stop position. Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, fails to disclose, teach or suggest this unique and innovative feature as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 5-7 of Applicant's claimed disclosure.

Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, does not disclose, teach or suggest any structure similar to Applicant's vehicle control system and vehicle control device as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 5-7 of Applicant's claimed disclosure. There is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. In fact, the cited references teach
away from and articulate various disadvantages associated with the arrangement, configuration and orientation of components taught in Applicant's claimed disclosure.

Thus, Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, does not disclose, teach or suggest Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 5-7 of Applicant's claimed disclosure. The deficiencies found in Poeppel et al. are not corrected by the combination of Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited. Additionally, there is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that amended independent Claims 1 and 5-7, and all claims depending directly or indirectly therefrom (Claims 2-4), are not obvious in light of and are patentable over Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that in view of Applicant's succinct arguments set forth above, Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, fails to disclose, teach or suggest several features that are recited in Applicant's claimed disclosure. As such, Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device are not disclosed, taught or suggested by Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited.
Without conceding to the correctness of the Examiner's comments thereto, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 2-4 are allowable, at least, for the same
reasons given above for amended independent Claim 1, because Claims 2-4 are ultimately dependent on Claim 1.

It is respectfully submitted that in view of Applicant's arguments stated above, Poeppel et al. is an improper primary reference, Wilson et al. is an improper secondary reference, and Applicant's claims are patentably distinct with respect thereto, as well as no teaching in existence to suggest the combination of any of the cited references. As set forth in MPEP § 2142, "the key to supporting any rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 is the clear articulation of the reason(s) why the claimed invention would have been obvious." As the U.S. Supreme Court noted in KSR Intl. Co. v. Teleflex Inc., "the analysis supporting a rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 should be made explicit." 82 USPQ2d 1385, 1396 (2007). The Federal Circuit has stated that "rejections on obviousness cannot be sustained by mere conclusory statements; instead, there must be some articulated reasoning with some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness." In re Kahn, 441 F.3d 977 at 988, 78 USPQ2d 1329 at 1336 (Fed. Cir. 2006). In the Office Action, the Examiner's conclusory statements are insufficient to establish a prima facie rejection because no articulated reasoning with rational underpinning was given, and no explanation as to exactly how the combination or modification could have been made was provided. As a result, Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner has failed to identify any motivation by one of ordinary skill in the art to combine or modify the art to arrive at the claimed disclosure other than the impermissible use of hindsight.
While it is Applicant's view that the claims as written are not obvious in light of the cited art and fully comply with Section 103, in the interest of advancing and expediting

prosecution, and without prejudice to pursuing this and related subject matter in future applications, Applicant has amended independent Claims 1 and 5-7. Therefore, amended independent Claims 1 and 5-7 should be in condition for allowance. Further, because Claims 2-4 depend from amended independent Claim 1, directly or indirectly, they are at least as limited, are similarly not taught by Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al. or any of the other references cited, and should also be in condition for allowance. In view of the above amendments and these remarks, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the Section 103 rejection to Claims 1-7.

New Claims 8-10 have been presented for the Examiner's consideration. Support for these new claims can be found throughout the specification, claims and drawings as originally filed. No new matter has been added. It is respectfully submitted that new dependent Claims 8-10 further help to define Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system, and its structural differences over the cited references.

Accordingly, in view of these remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that new Claims 8-10 are in condition for allowance. As such, Applicant respectfully requests favorable consideration of new Claims 8-10.
All of the stated grounds of rejection have been properly traversed, accommodated or rendered moot. Applicant therefore respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider

all presently outstanding rejections and that they be withdrawn. It is believed that a full and complete response has been made to the outstanding Office Action and, as such, the present application is in condition for allowance. Thus, prompt and favorable consideration of this Amendment is respectfully requested. If the Examiner believes that personal communication will expedite prosecution of this application, they are invited to contact the undersigned at their earliest convenience.
